item.title: Australia take control of final Ashes Test
item.description: Australia have taken control of the final Ashes Test against England's cricketers - closing the third day on 518 for 7. Steve Smith is unbeaten on 129. Travis Head also scored big, eventually falling for 163. Advertisement

item.title: Munster back-rowers out for trip to Toulon
item.description: Munster back-rowers John Hodnett and Alex Kendellen are both ruled out for Sunday's trip to Toulon. The province confirmed that Hodnett has undergone surgery on a thumb injury, while Kendellen is recovering from an ankle issue. Tighthead Oli Jager has returned to full training this week, but remains a doubt for this weekend's game in France. Advertisement

item.title: Under 20 and Minor Championship fixtures confirmed
item.description: Fixtures for the Munster Under 20 and Minor Football Championships have been confirmed. Dalata Hotel Group Under 20 champions Kerry will play their opening game away to the 2nd place team from Phase 1 on Thursday April 9th. Kerry will be away to Cork one week later, then host the 1st placed Phase 1 team on April 23rd. The final is on April 30th. item.title: Quartet to be inducted into Hall of Fame
item.description: Ken Black, Jerome Westbrooks, Michelle Fahy and Shane Coughlan will be inducted into Basketball Ireland's Hall of Fame in 2026. The quartet will formally take their place as the 23rd, 24th, 25th and 26th members of the prestigious hall at the Basketball Ireland Annual Awards ceremony on Saturday, May 23rd at The Osprey Hotel in Naas. item.title: Road in Cordal closed after truck jack-knifed in icy conditions
item.description: A road in Cordal is closed after a truck jack-knifed in icy conditions. The truck is blocking the road between Cordal village and Knocknaboul Cross. Kerry County Council says the truck will only be removed when it is safe to do so and the road is closed until further notice. Advertisement The council is also advising motorists that icy conditions persist in parts of east Kerry.

item.title: Valentia Coastguard responded to over 800 rescue call outs in 2025
item.description: Valentia Coastguard responded to over 800 rescue call outs last year. New figures show the Irish Coastguard responded to almost 3,000 incidents (2,793) in 2025, up 9.4% in a year. Valentia Marine Rescue coordinated 877 rescues, with helicopter support operating from Shannon, Dublin and Sligo. Advertisement Valentia Coastguard tasked the RNLI to incidents just under 800 (798) times, while it activated community inshore rescues services on 121 occasions. item.title: Kerry publicans calling for the introduction of a vaping ban in bars
item.description: Publicans in Kerry are calling for the introduction of a vaping ban in bars. An initiative by several pubs in the county, saw a joint decision to introduce a ban on vaping in their establishments on New Years Day. Listowel publican, Christy Walsh is among those who took the action; saying he has noticed an increase in people vaping in bars, while sitting at tables. item.title: Ruben Dias set to be out for up to 6 weeks
item.description: Manchester City are set to be without centre-back Ruben Dias for up to six weeks. Manager Pep Guardiola revealed the Portugal defender came off with an hamstring injury during Sunday's 1-all draw with Chelsea at the Etihad Stadium. City are now missing three of their central defenders, with John Stones and Josko Gvardiol also injured. item.title: Macroom Bypass reopened in both directions
item.description: The Macroom Bypass has reopened in both directions. It had been closed this morning following several collisions. Cork County Council says given recent freezing conditions, motorists are advised to drive with care. The council will continue to treat priority routes and other badly affected roads this evening and overnight. Advertisement
